title: The canonical coefficient morphisms $\alpha_f$, $\eta_f$
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring, let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of
schemes, and let $\Lambda_X$, $\Lambda_Y$ be the pulled-back coefficient rings
of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The pullback
$f^*\Lambda_Y$ and the pushforward $f_*\Lambda_X$ are ring objects: $f^*$ is
strong monoidal and $f_*$ is lax monoidal
([def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal],
[def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal]). Define
$$
\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow\Lambda_X,\qquad
\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow f_*\Lambda_X
$$
as follows.

- $\alpha_f$ is the component at $\Lambda$ of the natural isomorphism
  $f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp].
- $\eta_f$ is the mate of $\alpha_f$ under the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$: the
  unit $\Lambda_Y\to f_*f^*\Lambda_Y$ followed by $f_*\alpha_f$
  ([def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]).

Both are morphisms of ring objects. Moreover, $\alpha_f$ underlies an
isomorphism of ring objects $f^*\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$.

proof.text: Use the coefficient ring objects $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ and $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The functors $f^*$ and $f_*$ have respectively the strong and lax monoidal structures of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal], specialized to abelian sheaves. This specialization satisfies the hypotheses: [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] explicitly gives $\Ab$, with $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and unit $\mathbf Z$, as a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category and supplies the sheaf tensor products. Apply clause 1 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport] to each functor: for $F=f^*$ or $f_*$, the transported multiplication is $F(\mu)\circ\mu^F$ and the transported unit is $F(\eta)\circ\varepsilon^F$. Thus $f^*\Lambda_Y$ and $f_*\Lambda_X$ carry exactly the ring structures specified in the statement.

source.place: statement, first paragraph: transported ring structures

proof.text: Let $c_f:f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ be the comparison of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]. By [def-sfb-alpha], its component at $\Lambda$ has source $f^*p_Y^*\Lambda=f^*\Lambda_Y$ and target $p_X^*\Lambda=\Lambda_X$ and is precisely $\alpha_f$. This specifies the first map without choosing an inverse or a new comparison.

With the transported source ring structure fixed in step 1, [lem-sfb-alpha-ring-hom] says that this $\alpha_f$ preserves multiplication and unit. The isomorphism of ring objects in [def-sfb-alpha-bundled] first identifies the two ways of transporting $p_Y^*\Lambda$ along $f^*$ and then applies the component of the same comparison $c_f$. To check the first identification, write $F=p_Y^*$ and $G=f^*$. By the definition of the composite lax monoidal structure, both transported multiplications are $GF(\mu_\Lambda)\circ G(\mu^F_{\Lambda,\Lambda})\circ\mu^G_{F\Lambda,F\Lambda}$ and both units are $GF(\eta_\Lambda)\circ G(\varepsilon^F)\circ\varepsilon^G$. The identification therefore has underlying map $\mathrm{id}_{GF\Lambda}$. The underlying morphism of the bundled composite is $c_f(\Lambda)\circ\mathrm{id}_{GF\Lambda}$, hence $c_f(\Lambda)=\alpha_f$ as specified in step 2. Hence the claimed ring isomorphism has exactly the required underlying morphism.

source.place: First two sentences: alpha ring morphism and bundled ring isomorphism

proof.text: The adjunction of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], with $\mathcal A=\Ab$, has unit $u:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^*$. Define $\eta_f=f_*(\alpha_f)\circ u_{\Lambda_Y}$. By [def-sfb-eta] this is the stated mate of $\alpha_f$, with source $\Lambda_Y$ and target $f_*\Lambda_X$. In particular the mate is taken for the functors on abelian sheaves, before any change of scalars on module objects.

For the lax monoidal ring structure on $f_*\Lambda_X$ fixed in step 1, [lem-sfb-eta-ring-hom] asserts that the map $\eta_f$ of step 4 is a morphism of ring objects. Together with step 3 this establishes both ring-morphism assertions and the ring-isomorphism assertion for $\alpha_f$.
